newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss CPI shows no effect of easy SNB policy - CS.
newsitem.headline: Swiss CPI shows no effect of easy SNB policy - CS.

text.p: Swiss inflation in January was slightly higher than expected, but there are no signs of an inflationary effect from the Swiss National Bank's (SNB) easy monetary policy, economists at Credit Suisse said.

Even though January inflation was at the upper end of expectations, CS economists said in their Daily Focus trading letter that they would stick to their forecast for average 1997 inflation of 0.9 percent.
Swiss consumer prices rose 0.3 percent in January from December for a year-on-year rate of 0.8 percent, the Federal Statistics Office said earlier today.
"The weakening of the Swiss franc can slowly be seen in the rise in import prices," CS said.
Prices of domestic goods rose 0.3 percent in January for a year-on-year rate of 0.7 percent, while import prices rose 0.6 percent for a year-on-year rate of 1.2 percent.
"The CPI excluding oil products is evidence that the easier SNB monetary policy still has not had an inflationary effect," CS added.

Excluding oil products, the consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.3 percent in January for a year-on-year rise of 0.4 percent. Oil products rose 2.7 percent in January from December for a year-on-year rise of 16.1 percent.
CS economists had forecast January CPI would show a roughly 0.1 percent rise month-on-month and a 0.6 percent gain year-on-year.
Union Bank of Switzerland had forecast January inflation would be 0.2 percent month-on-month for a year-on-year rise of 0.7 percent.
